evidence: Nicollier 2015 primary note states equation (1) and explicitly conjectures that it has no exterior solution.
Abraham–Kovač, arXiv:1312.3176, accessible full-text material proves nonvanishing of the exterior field and derives the distance relation only from an interior stationary point.
correctness.rationale: For an exterior point \(P\), the elementary segment integral identity turns each logarithmic factor into the side integral \(J_a=\int_{BC}|P-Q|^{-1}\,ds\) and cyclic analogues. Applying the planar divergence theorem to \(Q\mapsto |P-Q|^{-1}\) gives \(E(P)=n_aJ_a+n_bJ_b+n_cJ_c\). Nicollier equality therefore gives \(J_a/a=J_b/b=J_c/c\), and the polygonal normal balance \(a n_a+b n_b+c n_c=0\) forces \(E(P)=0\). Strict separation of an exterior point from the compact convex triangle gives a unit vector \(u\) with \(u\cdot(P-Q)>0\) for every \(Q\) in the triangle, hence \(u\cdot E(P)>0\), contradiction. Boundary points are outside the quantified exterior domain and all side integrals are finite there.
risks: No computational certificate is needed; the only substantive sign convention is the outward-normal divergence identity, which was reconstructed directly.
